336 Metres to Checkpoint Two (and Why One Wheel Is at 94%)

Audience: Players and engineers interested in rally traversal, per-part suspension wear, and procedural track geometry

Content: observation

In Pipeline (liminal-pipeline), the stopwatch is the only opponent that matters. When you drop into Backbone Rally or a checkpoint sprint, the HUD pares down to three numbers in the top-left corner—your position (1st / 8), your lap timer (0:16.00), and the distance to the next glowing cyan gate (CP 2 · 336 m).

Look down at the bottom-left corner of Exhibit 2, though, and you can see why driving a vehicle in The Liminal feels different from sliding a single collision box along a track. Every rover is assembled from discrete parts—root, body, vector_t thrusters, and four individual wheel_sm corner assemblies—and each one carries its own structural state.

Come over a gravel crest too hot, land four degrees nose-low on the front-right corner, and the main chassis (body 100/100) shrugs it off while that single overloaded wheel takes the brunt of the impact (wheel_sm 94/100). Nobody fired a shot at you; the terrain itself has teeth if you mistime a jump.

The Mystery of the 75-Centimetre Rail Bump

Building Backbone Rally (Exhibit 3) also forced us to track down one of our favourite terrain bugs of the autumn: an invisible step on an elevated coaster rail that launched rovers into the air at the exact same coordinate (X = -149, Z = 571) on some runs and let them glide past on others.

Our rail generator builds elevated tracks and carved roadbeds by stamping height changes onto the terrain grid. Originally, it walked the spline segment by segment:

• Take segment i from point $A$ to point $B$.
• For every terrain cell within the rail's 2.0 m half-width, blend the ground height toward the rail elevation.
• Move to segment i + 1 and repeat.

That worked until two segments met at a slight bend near (-149, 571). A terrain sample sitting right on the 2.0 m edge of the rail had a squared distance of 3.9995806 m² when evaluated by the standalone .NET server, and 4.00015211 m² when evaluated by Unity's Mono runtime—a difference of half a micrometre right at the 2.0² = 4.0 m² cutoff.

Because each segment was stamped onto the heightfield one after another, that single boundary cell was included by one runtime and skipped by the other, leaving a 0.75 m vertical lip across the rail bed. At rally speeds, hitting a 75-centimetre step is the difference between a 3.67s personal best and losing a wheel assembly.

Stamping the Whole Ribbon at Once

Once we saw the numbers side by side, the fix was both simpler and cleaner than tweaking floating-point tolerances:

• One polyline query per cell: Instead of modifying the terrain grid inside a per-segment loop where Segment $A$ changes the ground before Segment $B$ reads it, every terrain cell now queries its minimum distance to the entire continuous rail polyline first, and applies a single smooth elevation blend.
• Infrastructure order as law: Rivers carve the valley first, roads and bridges grade their approaches across the water second, and coaster rails stamp last.

Now, when you bank toward Checkpoint 2 at sixty kilometres an hour, the only bumps under your wheels are the ones the track designer actually put there.

Attribution: observer: Eric Lortie; textGenerator: Liminal Editorial Workshop; editor: Eric Lortie

Limitations: Captures and rail-boundary telemetry reflect liminal-pipeline checkpoint and Backbone Rally circuits.

# 336 Metres to Checkpoint Two \(and Why One Wheel Is at 94%\)

Audience: Players and engineers interested in rally traversal, per-part suspension wear, and procedural track geometry

Content: observation

![Three-quarter close-up of the wheeled Backbone Rally rover showing its four articulated silver wheel\_sm corner assemblies on the road](https://ericlortie.github.io/liminal-blyg/media/4ee57bbcc1e4fe1ab3487674471dfb4bb5775b978b0fc72e4ad632df922699db.png)

Exhibit 1 — Close three-quarter view of the wheeled rally rover \(base:procgen\_warwagon\): a modular chassis \(root, body, vector\_t\) riding on four independent wheel\_sm corner assemblies, with two rival rovers lining up along the road grade behind it.

![Chase view looking down the carved highway past three wheeled rally rovers toward the glowing cyan gate under volumetric clouds](https://ericlortie.github.io/liminal-blyg/media/984a0714e3fa85e67ee24e0b791af506e8be4115c4497137e673e9eddf4b8e4e.png)

Exhibit 2 — Looking down a continuous stamped road corridor in liminal-pipeline as three rally rovers sprint toward the glowing cyan portal gate beneath volumetric cloud bands and purple aurora.

![Low ground-skim side profile of the wheeled rover riding the road surface](https://ericlortie.github.io/liminal-blyg/media/2b0f5329df571d5b0020fed17818ee8c72cddc153fb6e70226bb49b1754c7ff1.png)
